claims: For the specified periodic suitable weak solution smooth before an interior candidate terminal time, finite local spacetime L^(5/2) rank-one defect implies regularity at that point. The dimensionless integral includes nu^(-3/2).

A terminal-slice covering argument produces a solution-dependent regular collar. Exact localized enstrophy retains its transport and viscous cutoff flux, controlled in L1 time by collar velocity and the existing dissipation, not by unproved pressure or vorticity derivative bounds.

Critical Young absorption and Gronwall give interior vorticity L-infinity-time L2-space control, which matches GKT's p=q=2 local vorticity criterion. The same scoped proof accepts finite critical positive effective stretching rate.

The elementary inequality abs(lambda2(sym A)) <= dist_F(A,rank<=1) identifies overlap with known local spectral criteria. The checked NP theorem retains Dirichlet and interior-open-set assumptions; it is not directly relabeled a periodic one-sided terminal theorem.
limitations: No arbitrary-data global regularity, singularity construction, novelty certification, human peer review or Clay solution.
No unconditional local critical defect norm or prescribed-centre good scale is obtained.
The proved local estimate has solution-dependent collar and initial-slice constants. A uniform quantitative epsilon-regularity scale is not established.
The direct enstrophy proof is not an arbitrary-local-suitable-weak theorem: smooth-preterminal testing and the specified suitable continuation are explicit.
The proposed single-scale L2-defect criterion, general weak rank-one limit regularity, and quantitative pressure/regularity transfer remain open.
